chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, all from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from Ali ibn Ri'ab, from Abu Hamza, who said:

I heard Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) saying: When a man marries a thayyib (previously married) woman who had been married to another husband, and she alleges that he did not come near her since he entered into marriage with her, then the word regarding that is the word of the man, and upon him is to swear by Allah that he has copulated with her, because she is the plaintiff.

He (peace be upon him) said: So if he married her and she was a virgin, and she claims that he did not reach her, then in a situation like this, women know (how to determine), so let her be examined by the one who is reliable from among them. So when she mentions that she is a virgin, then it is upon the Imam to delay him for a year. So if he reached her, or else there would be a separation between the two, and she would be given half the dower, and there would be no waiting period upon her.

key_terms.الثَّيِّب: A woman who has been previously married and consummated her marriage
key_terms.عِدَّة: Waiting period for a woman after divorce or death of husband
key_terms.يَقْرَبْهَا: To come near her (euphemism for sexual intercourse)

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic legal ruling on proving consummation of marriage when a husband and wife dispute it?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi details the jurisprudential distinction in proving consummation (wusul) between a previously married woman (thayyib) and a virgin (bakr), reflecting the Shia emphasis on evidentiary standards in marital disputes. For a virgin, the procedure involves examination by a trustworthy woman and a one-year waiting period (ajl) to verify virginity, after which the husband pays half the dowry if consummation is not proven. This ruling underscores the practical application of burden of proof in family law, ensuring fairness in financial settlements and marital status determination.
